organism_context: Streptomyces aureofaciens (chlortetracycline cluster); characterised as OxyQ in Streptomyces rimosus oxytetracycline biosynthesis, and all essential oxy enzymes have ctc homologues
rationale: Heterologous reconstitution showed OxyL/OxyQ/OxyT perform C-12a hydroxylation, C-4 amination and C-4 N,N-dimethylation respectively; adding OxyQ alone to a 4-keto-anhydrotetracycline-producing strain gave 4-amino-anhydrotetracycline, a single amino-transfer activity. KEGG R09199 itself no longer resolves (404), so the entry is orphaned upstream as well.
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux is 4-oxo to 4-amino (the council's direction); the amine donor that commits the reaction is absent from the equation entirely, so no N balance and no direction signal survives.

organism_context: Streptomyces aureofaciens chlortetracycline pathway; characterised as OxyT in S. rimosus
rationale: OxyT is a SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase shown in vitro to convert 4-amino-anhydrotetracycline to anhydrotetracycline; the two methyl transfers occur at the same C-4 amine, i.e. one catalytic activity used twice, not two activities.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible in the methylation direction, which is left-to-right as written; KEGG R09200 has also been withdrawn (404).

enzyme_name: Epoxide hydrolase (bacterial EphA/EphB-type in PAH degraders; microsomal EH in mammals)
organism_context: Mycobacterium vanbaalenii-type benzo[a]pyrene degraders (KEGG rn00624); the same chemistry in mammals is run by microsomal EH
rationale: KEGG annotates R09211 only as 'epoxide hydrolase' (EC 3.3.2.-), so the specific protein is inferred from the chemistry; every alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold epoxide hydrolase that makes trans-dihydrodiols carries a single catalytic activity. The genuinely bifunctional member of this family is the soluble EH (EPHX2, phosphatase + hydrolase), which is not the enzyme acting here.
direction_note: Hydrolytic epoxide ring opening is irreversible; no enzyme re-forms an arene oxide from the trans-diol, so ModelSEED's reverse direction has no enzymatic basis.

organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. B13 / P. cepacia and other chloro- and methyl-aromatic degraders using the modified ortho-cleavage pathway
rationale: Dienelactone hydrolase purified from Pseudomonas sp. B13 is a ~28 kDa monomeric cysteine hydrolase whose only activity is converting dienelactones to maleylacetates; the 3-chloro-2-methyl substrate is the same chemistry on a substituted ring.
direction_note: Lactone hydrolysis to the free dicarboxylate is irreversible in vivo and the enzyme has no lactonising activity, so the forward (hydrolytic) call is the enzymologically supported one.

organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. P51/B13 and related chloroaromatic degraders; a distinct Rhodococcus opacus 1CP ClcB2 lineage does the same job
rationale: Cl-MLE is an enolase-superfamily cycloisomerase in which the lactonisation and the chloride elimination take place as one transformation in one active site, so it is monofunctional rather than bifunctional.
direction_note: Loss of chloride makes the cycloisomerisation to the dienelactone effectively one-way, i.e. left-to-right as written, which is the council's call.

organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. B13 / P. cepacia and other chloro- and methyl-aromatic degraders
rationale: Same enzyme as for the 3-chloro-2-methyl isomer: a monomeric single-activity cysteine hydrolase (EC 3.1.1.45, KEGG K01061) that opens dienelactones to maleylacetates.
direction_note: Hydrolytic ring opening is irreversible; there is no enzymatic route back from the maleylacetate to the lactone.

enzyme_name: 3-Oxoadipate enol-lactone hydrolase (enol-lactonase PcaD/CatD), acting on the 4-methyl substrate
organism_context: Standalone PcaD/CatD in Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter (MetaCyc assigns PWY-6185 to Pseudomonas); in Rhodococcus opacus 1CP and other actinobacteria the identical activity sits on the fused bifunctional PcaL
rationale: KEGG labels R09226 '4-methyl-3-oxoadipate-enol-lactone hydrolase' (EC 3.1.1.24-type), a beta-ketoadipate-pathway alpha/beta hydrolase that is a separate polypeptide in the proteobacterial hosts this 4-methylcatechol pathway is curated to. Lineage caveat recorded rather than applied: in R. opacus 1CP pcaD is fused to pcaC, giving the bifunctional PcaL (4-carboxymuconolactone decarboxylase + enol-lactone hydrolase), whose two activities could not be chromatographically separated.
direction_note: Enol-lactone hydrolysis is irreversible; the Rhodococcus PcaL fusion would not change the direction of this half-reaction.

organism_context: Sphingobium sp. SYK-6 (formerly Sphingomonas paucimobilis SYK-6)
rationale: DesA is the H4folate-dependent O-demethylase converting syringate to 3-O-methylgallate (KEGG K15064); it is a single-activity methyl-transfer enzyme, 49% identical to the related demethylase LigM.
direction_note: This is a committed catabolic demethylation feeding the 3MGA pathway; remethylating 3-O-methylgallate from 5-methyl-THF is not a physiological reaction, so ModelSEED's reverse direction is wrong.

organism_context: Sphingobium sp. SYK-6 (formerly Sphingomonas paucimobilis SYK-6)
rationale: Crude LigM converts vanillate to protocatechuate and 3-O-methylgallate to gallate with similar specific activities and only in the presence of H4folate, and a ligM mutant completely loses 3MGA O-demethylase activity: two substrates, one catalytic activity.
direction_note: Catabolic demethylation toward gallate is the physiological direction (left-to-right here); the reverse O-methylation of gallate by 5-methyl-THF is not an activity of LigM.

enzyme_name: none - KEGG flags R09274 as spontaneous
organism_context: 3-O-methylgallate 4,5-ring-cleavage pathway (Sphingobium SYK-6 and relatives)
rationale: KEGG R09274 carries the explicit COMMENT 'spontaneous': the LigAB ring-fission product of 3-O-methylgallate lactonises to 2-pyrone-4,6-dicarboxylate with loss of methanol non-enzymatically, so there is no catalysing protein to classify as mono- or bifunctional.
direction_note: The spontaneous intramolecular transesterification runs one way (toward the pyrone + methanol), which matches the council's call, but no enzyme sets this direction.

enzyme_name: Aclacinomycin deoxysugar glycosyltransferase (L-rhodinosyl transfer onto aclacinomycin S; AknK the leading candidate)
organism_context: Streptomyces galilaeus aclacinomycin biosynthetic cluster
rationale: Aclacinomycin S (C36H45NO13) to aclacinomycin N (C42H55NO15) is addition of one L-rhodinose unit, so the catalyst must be a single-domain GT-B deoxysugar glycosyltransferase; KEGG assigns R09333 no EC and no KO, and in the reconstituted pathway AknK (EC 2.4.1.327, otherwise the 2-deoxyfucosyltransferase) supplied the third sugar at low levels. AknOx, the dual-active-site flavoenzyme of this cluster, acts downstream on aclacinomycin N and is not the enzyme for this step.
direction_note: The NDP-sugar donor and the NDP product are both absent from the equation; their release is what makes glycosyl transfer irreversible in the biosynthetic (left-to-right) direction, and stripping them is what let the estimators flip the call.

organism_context: Streptomyces purpurascens / S. violaceus rhodomycin producers
rationale: KEGG annotates R09336 as 'glycosyltransferase, rdmH, rhoG' and the mass difference between epsilon-rhodomycinone (C22H20O9) and epsilon-rhodomycin T (C30H35NO11) is exactly one rhodosamine unit, i.e. one glycosyl-transfer activity. No literature bearing on bi- or polyfunctionality of RdmH/RhoG was found, and the protein identity rests on the KEGG annotation alone.
direction_note: The TDP-L-rhodosamine donor is missing from the equation; glycosyl transfer with NDP release runs forward (aglycone to glycoside), which is the council's direction.

organism_context: mer operon of mercury-resistant bacteria; also expressed heterologously in mammalian cells
rationale: MerB is a small single-domain lyase that cleaves the Hg-C bond by protonolysis using two strictly conserved active-site cysteines; it has one catalytic activity and passes Hg(II) to the physically separate polypeptide MerA (a two-protein system, not a fusion).
direction_note: Protonolysis releasing methane is irreversible - no enzyme methylates Hg(II) using methane - so ModelSEED's reverse direction would imply CH4-driven mercury methylation, which does not exist.

organism_context: Streptomyces argillaceus mithramycin pathway
rationale: MtmW is a tetrameric NADPH-dependent aldo-keto reductase that reduces the distal keto group of the mithramycin DK side chain - one catalytic activity; its immediate product is iso-mithramycin, which isomerises to mithramycin non-enzymatically via Mg2+, so KEGG's single entry also hides a spontaneous step.
direction_note: The reduction is driven by NADPH, which the equation omits (only two bare H+ remain); removing the hydride donor is exactly what lets the thermodynamic estimators flip this to reverse.

organism_context: Linum usitatissimum (flax)
rationale: LuHNL conserves the substrate- and NAD(H)-binding domains of Zn2+-dependent alcohol dehydrogenase and binds an A-form NAD+ tightly in each subunit, yet there is no evidence it has ADH activity; cyanohydrin cleavage via a cyano-zinc complex is its sole catalytic function.
direction_note: HNLs are freely reversible and are used preparatively in the condensation direction for (R)-cyanohydrin synthesis; in planta the net flux is cyanogenic cleavage (the council's direction), driven by HCN escape and substrate supply rather than by the enzyme.

organism_context: mammalian (rat/human) liver microsomes
rationale: KEGG assigns R09410 to K01253 / EC 3.3.2.9, microsomal EH, a single-activity alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold enzyme (its reported bile-acid-transport role is non-catalytic moonlighting). Caveat for the reaction rather than the enzyme: AFB1-exo-8,9-epoxide hydrolyses extremely rapidly without catalysis, so much of this flux is spontaneous.
direction_note: Epoxide hydration is irreversible - the reverse would require regenerating a highly reactive epoxide from a stable diol - so the council's forward call is the enzymologically supported one.

organism_context: mammalian aflatoxin B1 metabolism (chemistry, not enzymology)
rationale: AFB1 dihydrodiol undergoes a base-catalysed rearrangement to, and sits in equilibrium with, the AFB1 dialdehyde; KEGG gives R09411 no EC and no orthology, so there is no catalysing enzyme to classify.
direction_note: This is a pH-dependent spontaneous equilibrium, so neither a forward nor a reverse constraint is enzymologically justified; net flow toward the dialdehyde is set by its consumption (lysine adduction, AKR7A reduction).

organism_context: rat (AKR7A1) and human (AKR7A2/AKR7A3) liver
rationale: KEGG assigns R09412 to K15303, aflatoxin B1 aldehyde reductase; AFAR is a single-domain aldo-keto reductase that reduces the AFB1 dialdehyde to its mono- and dialcohols. Its broad carbonyl substrate range (e.g. succinic semialdehyde) is one activity on many substrates, not a second activity.
direction_note: The reduction is NADPH-driven and physiologically irreversible, but the equation keeps only two bare H+; with the hydride donor deleted the direction call has nothing to anchor it.

organism_context: rat (AKR7A1) and human (AKR7A2/AKR7A3) liver
rationale: Same enzyme as R09412, reducing the other aldehyde of the AFB1 dialdehyde to give the regioisomeric monoalcohol; AFAR is a single-activity aldo-keto reductase.
direction_note: NADPH is missing from the equation (only two H+ remain), which is what allows the direction to be inverted; the real NADPH-dependent reduction runs left-to-right.

organism_context: rat (AKR7A1) and human (AKR7A2/AKR7A3) liver
rationale: Second reduction by the same AFAR enzyme, converting the AFB1 monoalcohol to the dialcohol; recombinant AKR7A1/AKR7A3 reduce the dialdehyde to both mono- and dialcohols, one catalytic activity acting twice.
direction_note: NADPH, the species that makes this reduction irreversible, is absent from the equation.

organism_context: rat (AKR7A1) and human (AKR7A2/AKR7A3) liver
rationale: Same AFAR aldo-keto reductase reducing the alternative monoalcohol regioisomer to the common AFB1 dialcohol; single catalytic activity.
direction_note: NADPH is stripped from the equation, leaving only two H+, so the direction call rests on nothing; the enzymatic reduction runs left-to-right.

organism_context: mammalian liver microsomes (rat/human)
rationale: EC 3.3.2.9 / EPHX1 is a single-activity alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold enzyme that opens arene oxides such as DMBA-5,6-oxide to trans-dihydrodiols; its reported bile-acid-transport role is non-catalytic moonlighting, and the genuinely bifunctional family member is the soluble EH EPHX2 (N-terminal lipid phosphatase + C-terminal hydrolase), which is not this enzyme.
direction_note: Epoxide hydration is irreversible; there is no enzymatic dehydration of a trans-dihydrodiol back to the arene oxide.

distinct_activities: N-terminal domain: Mg2+-dependent ionisation/cyclisation of (2E,6E)-farnesyl diphosphate to germacradienol (+ germacrene D) with PPi release - germacradienol synthase, EC 4.2.3.22
C-terminal domain: protonation-dependent retro-Prins fragmentation/Prins cyclisation of germacradienol to geosmin + acetone - EC 4.1.99.16
organism_context: Streptomyces coelicolor and other actinobacteria; a bifunctional alpha-alpha terpene synthase. Fungal geosmin producers also use a bifunctional cyclase.
rationale: Crystallographic and mutagenesis work shows ScGS has two distinct metal-dependent active sites on one polypeptide: the N-terminal domain cyclises FPP to germacradienol, and the C-terminal domain fragments germacradienol to geosmin and acetone - two genuine catalytic activities, not a moonlighting role or a subunit complex.
direction_note: This entry is the C-terminal domain's retro-Prins fragmentation, which expels acetone and is irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse call (geosmin + acetone to germacradienol) has no enzymatic counterpart, and the bifunctionality is precisely why the committed step upstream (FPP ionisation) never appears in this equation.

organism_context: Methanosarcina acetivorans (Methanosarcinales/Methanomicrobiales coenzyme M pathway); the protein evolved from an ancestral threonine synthase by gene duplication
rationale: The MA3297 PLP protein specifically catalyses the beta-replacement of L-phosphoserine + sulfite to L-cysteate + Pi and does NOT complement an E. coli thrC mutant or run the threonine synthase reaction - the ancestral activity was lost, so this is a monofunctional enzyme and not a bifunctional cysteate/threonine synthase.
direction_note: Nucleophilic addition of sulfite to a PLP-bound dehydroalanine with phosphate release is a committed biosynthetic step toward coenzyme M, i.e. left-to-right as written; ModelSEED's reverse direction would have the cell making phosphoserine from cysteate.

organism_context: fungal: Aspergillus oryzae (AoRut), A. niger, Acremonium sp. DSM 24697
rationale: Rutinosidases are single-catalytic-domain glycoside hydrolases that release the intact rutinose disaccharide from hesperidin in one step (the crystal structure of A. oryzae AoRut shows one active site); their transglycosylation is the same chemistry with a non-water acceptor, not a second activity. Crude commercial 'hesperidinase' is a mixture of separate alpha-rhamnosidase and beta-glucosidase proteins, which is a preparation, not a bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is strongly favoured in vivo; the condensation direction is only accessible in vitro at high sugar/acceptor concentration, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is wrong.
